description: Sort the entries of array in place, ordered by compareFn, or, with no compareFn, as < orders them, and return the same array, as in ECMAScript. The sort is stable: entries that compare equal keep their order. With no compareFn, every entry must be of one data type (a mix is an error, as it is for <); unlike ECMAScript, entries are not converted to strings, so [10, 9, 1] sorts to [1, 9, 10]. NaN has no order, so it is an error. With compareFn, the array may hold any mix of data types. Undefined entries go last and are not compared, as in ECMAScript. A frozen array is an error before compareFn is called. Use to_sorted for a sorted copy.

parameters.description: The array to sort. Must not be frozen.
parameters.name: array

parameters.description: Called with two defined entries, once per comparison. If omitted, entries are ordered as < orders them. Return true, or a negative integer, when a sorts before b; false, zero or a positive integer otherwise. Entries that compare equal keep their order. Any other result, a double included, is an error.
parameters.name: compareFn

sideEffects: The array is sorted in place.
